title: U.S. Space Force adds second surveillance sensor to Japanese constellation
summary: The U.S. Space Force launched QZS-7 on Aug. 10, adding a second surveillance sensor to Japan's navigation satellite constellation as part of a bilateral program. This completes the initiative to host U.S. sensors aboard Japanese navigation satellites.

title: Wallops gears up for an increase in launches
summary: Wallops Island is preparing for a significant increase in launches, prompting calls for infrastructure improvements to support companies and workers. This surge in activity is expected to drive economic and operational benefits for the space industry.

title: Spire and PlanetiQ win NOAA radio-occultation contracts
summary: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) awarded contracts to Spire Global and PlanetiQ for providing radio occultation data to support terrestrial and space weather forecasts. This partnership aims to enhance weather prediction capabilities using advanced satellite data.

title: Cheaper launch has moved the spacecraft bottleneck. Mass is out, surface area is in.
summary: Cheaper launch costs have shifted the primary constraint in spacecraft design from mass to surface area. This change emphasizes the need for innovative solutions to optimize spacecraft surface configurations.

title: Blue Origin outlines plans for second Cape Canaveral launch pad
summary: Blue Origin announced plans to expand its Florida launch site by adding a second pad for a larger version of New Glenn. The company aims to rebuild and enhance its Cape Canaveral facilities.

title: CesiumAstro buys semiconductor specialist to boost constellation plans

title: Space Force awards five companies $60 million for multi-vendor satellite network tests
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded five companies a total of $60 million to prototype and test connections to a SpaceX-built data network backbone for a multi-vendor satellite network. The companies involved are Amazon Leo, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Rocket Lab, and York Space.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 223 — The Lunar Domain
